thread:
Martin (Support): Hey team, incoming escalation from a customer using our hosted API via an IDE plugin. They see persistent broken pipes during streaming and they're being billed as 5xx. Sample: trace 8f3a7b2a. Repro steps attached below.

Priya (eng-runtime): thanks Martin — can you paste a minimal curl or trace and the request headers? is this using chunked transfer / Transfer-Encoding: chunked?

Martin (Support): Yep. Plugin opens a streaming connection and writes client-side chunks intermittently. Minimal repro: 

Martin (Support): ```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" \
  -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/generate \
  --data-binary $'4\r\ntest\r\n0\r\n\r\n'
```

Martin (Support): From the customer logs: `EPIPE: write ECONNRESET` and our gateway logs show: `upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header` then we mark the call as 502.

Diego (eng-sre): throwing this on the thread — how frequent? transient or spike?

Martin (Support): Happens ~5-10% of IDE sessions, customer reports spike when plugin does long pauses between client chunks (~10-30s).

Priya (eng-runtime): that pause is suspicious — our streaming runtime expects the client to keep the socket alive. We have keepalive/idle timeout on the proxy layer (envoy/nginx) and also our idle KV cache flush. Do we have a sample gateway trace (X-Request-Id)?

Martin (Support): yes: x-req-id=8f3a7b2a (same trace above). I pulled the gateway request log: `t=2025-08-01T18:12:34Z method=POST path=/v1/streams/generate status=502 upstream_status=- upstream_time=0.003s` and worker logs show `write failed: Broken pipe (EPIPE)`.

Priya (eng-runtime): ok. Diego — can you check proxy idle timeouts and whether half-close behavior vs FIN+RST is being propagated? Some client libs do a `shutdown(SHUT_WR)` which can be interpreted differently by the proxy and might drop the upstream prematurely.

Diego (eng-sre): looking. I also want to confirm how we classify these into billing. Yuki, I think billing picked these up as 5xx and flagged for charging.

Yuki (billing): I saw a spike in 502-marked streaming sessions yesterday for that account. We currently bill on completed-response tokens unless status >= 500 then flagged separately. If gateway marks as 502 we treat as provider error and may not bill, but Support escalations claim they were billed. Need to reconcile.

Priya (eng-runtime): potential hypothesis: client silent pause -> proxy times out -> proxy returns a 502 to client (or closes) -> client library treats it as an abort and retries -> our gateway sees partial bytes and counts as 5xx in metrics, but billing pipeline consumed token counters earlier (we meter tokens as they're produced by the model). That can cause mismatch: user billed for tokens produced but request label is 5xx.

Martin (Support): Customer insists they were billed and got no data for some requests. They provided a request id and invoice line items (attached).

Diego (eng-sre): I'm pulling the envoy config now. Notable parameters: upstream_idle_timeout=20s, proxy_write_timeout=30s. Customer pause ~25s -> likely hit the 20s idle path.

Priya (eng-runtime): that matches. We should short-circuit: either increase idle timeout for streaming routes or implement application-level keepalive (heartbeats) for long-pauses. But we also need to avoid long-lived resource usage.

Diego (eng-sre): quick mitigation: bump upstream_idle_timeout to 60s for /v1/streams/* route in the gateway. Will test in staging then prod canary.

deploy-bot: Deployment queued: change envoy config upstream_idle_timeout=60s for route /v1/streams/* (change set #R-5542). Planned rollouts: staging -> canary (5%) -> full.

Priya (eng-runtime): also, we should consider changing how we detect client disconnects vs proxy-induced closures. Right now our error classifier treats `io.EPIPE` during write to client as a 5xx if the upstream didn't complete. For chunked clients that pause, we should not classify as provider 5xx if model produced tokens earlier. Suggest: annotate meter events with final response outcome only after upstream completes, and switch to marking these as 'client_abort' when client closed first (requires correlation with socket close flags).

Yuki (billing): For immediate billing reconciliation, we can run a one-off job to find traces where tokens were consumed but status=5xx and reverse-bill or credit customer. Send me the list of x-req-ids.

Martin (Support): sending as DM: 8f3a7b2a, 8f3c11ff, 8f4b00aa (customer provided sample set).

Diego (eng-sre): staging test: reproduced with a small script that writes first chunk, sleeps 25s, writes second chunk. Envoy on staging returned `502` at 20s and then upstream got `EPIPE`. Confirmed.

Priya (eng-runtime): good repro. For the runtime fix we can also add a small keepalive ping frame the server expects if client silence > 15s. But that would require client-side update for plugin. So immediate path is proxy timeout bump + billing reconciliation. Mid-term: update error classification and docs for streaming contract (recommended heartbeat every 10s).

Diego (eng-sre): rolling canary now (5%). Observability: watch 502 rate for streaming route, also watch open socket counts.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for change #R-5542 (5% traffic).

Diego (eng-sre): Canary looks clean at 5%. No surge in connection count, 502s for streaming route fell from 3.8% -> 0.4% on canary hosts.

Priya (eng-runtime): thanks. I'll open a follow-up to instrument socket close reasons in the runtime logs so we can deterministically label client vs proxy vs upstream failures.

Yuki (billing): I pulled the three traces. Two of them have tokens produced and charged despite status=502. I'll flag those invoices for a credit. For broader customers, we should run weekly audit of token-charge vs final-status mismatches for last 30d.

Martin (Support): Customer notified and appreciative for quick triage. They asked if we can provide a recommended heartbeat for the IDE plugin. Priya, can you draft a one-paragraph guidance?

Priya (eng-runtime): sure — TL;DR: send a small keepalive chunk at least every 10s while the client expects the stream to remain open; set Transfer-Encoding: chunked; handle mid-stream 5xx by retrying idempotent prompts. I'll push to docs and DM you a short snippet.

Diego (eng-sre): Once we finish canary -> full deploy I'll close this. Also adding an alert to paging if streaming 502 rate > 1% for more than 5m.

Martin (Support): closing loop: prod fully rolled out at 2025-08-01T20:34:48Z, billing credits issued to customer for the samples, docs updated. Customer still planning to add ping in plugin. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Yuki (billing): marking resolved from billing side.

Priya (eng-runtime): creating follow-up issue to change error classifier and add socket-close provenance tag (TASK-789).

Diego (eng-sre): drafting runbook entry for streaming timeouts + recommended envoy settings.

Martin (Support): ok moving to resolved. Will reopen if customer sees recurrence.
